lines.text: [softly] Go. I will be in the stone.
Walk carefully. The dead remember the living.
[sighs] Until the next stone.
The night will come again. Be ready for it.

lines.ask: (every prompt in a topic already heard)
lines.text: [softly] I have told you all I know of that. For now.

lines.ask: (every prompt in a topic already heard)
lines.text: Nothing more... not yet. Free another stone, and I may remember more.
[softly] Helgen burned. The World-Eater flew north over the smoke... and as he flew, he shouted into the earth.
Three words. SLEN... TIID... VO. Flesh. Time. Undo. The shout he raises his dragons with.
But this time it fell on every grave in Skyrim. And every grave heard it.

lines.ask: Why do the dead come back?
lines.text: His shout hangs like a mist over every road the dead walk. Shor's hall, Arkay's mercy, whatever waits for them... none of them can pass it.

lines.ask: Why do the dead come back?
lines.text: [sad] They try, every night. The mist turns them back... and his voice throws them down to Skyrim again, as red light out of the sky.

lines.ask: What are the red beams in the sky?
lines.text: The dead, falling. Turned back from Sovngarde, and thrown down wherever his voice is strongest.

lines.ask: What are the red beams in the sky?
lines.text: [tense] The red lightning is worse. That is how the strong ones come... the ones his voice holds tightest.
Echo Altars. The old Tongues raised one in every hold, long before your Empire, to answer a dragon's voice with their own.
When the World-Eater shouted, they went dark. Wake one, and its city's dead will sleep again.

lines.ask: How do I wake an altar?
lines.text: [whispers] ...four trials... at night... the dead... the stone will show you...

lines.ask: How do I wake an altar?
lines.text: ...one city at a time... and then I will be clearer...
You have a dragon's soul in a mortal's body. When you kill one of the dead, the stone hears it the way it hears a shout.
The Tongues would have given anything to be what you are. [softly] Do not waste it.
What is left of his shout in the dead. When they fall, it comes out of them... and it comes to you.
The stone can make it into steel, and spells, and brews. Spend it. It does no good in your pocket.
The dead will drag you down. If anyone stands with you, they can lift you again. If no one does... [pause] the night ends without you.
Do not let it. I have lost enough people to the dark.

lines.ask: What is the Tablet of Mysteries?
lines.text: An old thing, and a strange one. The Tongues left weapons with it that they did not want to keep.

lines.ask: What is the Tablet of Mysteries?
lines.text: Feed it the essence, and it will give you one. It does not tell you which. [softly] Neither will I.

lines.ask: Why do the cities teach me shouts?
lines.text: Every freed city remembers a little of the Voice. They teach it to the one who freed them.

lines.ask: Why do the cities teach me shouts?
lines.text: Use them. A shout is a weapon the dead cannot answer.
Two stones awake, and their voices carry to each other. That is how you hear me now.
Every stone you wake makes the mist thinner. Not gone... but thinner.

lines.ask: Why one city at a time?
lines.text: Each altar answers for its own hold. The dead of Whiterun do not care that Riverwood sleeps.

lines.ask: Why one city at a time?
lines.text: And each city has its keeper. A priest who swore an oath to the World-Eater... and remembers it.
Men who served the dragons when the dragons ruled. They wore masks of the dragons' faces, and took the dragons' power.
[bitter] When the shout came, every one of them woke with his oath still in his mouth. They keep the altars dark for their master.
Break a city's seals, and its priest must come out to face you.
Four stones. Five. The mist trembles when the sixth wakes... I can feel it already.
At six... I will be able to tell you who I am. And something old will begin to stir.
The wonders. Four weapons, one for each path, hidden when the Tongues still walked. They sleep no longer.
Each waits for the one who walks its path. But none of them will simply be found. Each must be earned.
When yours is won, the Greybeards will call you to the mountain. The wonder waits beneath their hall.

lines.ask: What do the Greybeards have to do with this?
lines.text: High Hrothgar sits on the Throat of the World. Where the Tongues cast the World-Eater out of time.

lines.ask: What do the Greybeards have to do with this?
lines.text: Beneath it is a room the Greybeards guard and do not speak of. The wonders are kept there, until they are won.

lines.ask: What is the echo on the summit?
lines.text: When we cast him out of time, his voice did not all go with him. Part of it stayed behind, caught on the summit where we broke him.

lines.ask: What is the echo on the summit?
lines.text: It has circled there since, waiting. Now that he is back in the world, it answers him... and it is louder than ever.

lines.ask: What is the echo on the summit?
lines.text: He flies where he likes. The echo cannot leave the mountain. That is why you can reach it... and why breaking it breaks his hold on the dead.

lines.ask: Every altar is awake. Is it over?
lines.text: [softly] Every stone sings again. Listen... all of Skyrim answering at once. I have not heard that in a very long time.

lines.ask: Every altar is awake. Is it over?
lines.text: But the World-Eater's voice is not gone. It lingers in the wild places... and in the echo he left on the summit.

lines.ask: Every altar is awake. Is it over?
lines.text: The cities are safe. The rest of Skyrim is not. Not yet.

lines.ask: The wonders are won. What now?
lines.text: [tense] Now the words wake. Each of the three words of his shout was carried by a dragon. They are flying again.

lines.ask: The wonders are won. What now?
lines.text: SLEN in the Reach. TIID under Labyrinthian. VO on the peak of Mount Anthor. Silence all three.

lines.ask: The wonders are won. What now?
lines.text: Each will come at night, with a siege of the dead before it. And each one gives back what it stole.
Slenvahrin. The Flesh-Wyrm. It circles the cult's old shrine in the Reach, and the barrow-dead around it grow new flesh.
Kill it, and the strength the World-Eater poured into the dead will run in you instead.
Tiidrah. The Time-Wyrm. It sleeps under Labyrinthian, where the cult laid its dead by the thousand.
It gives the dead back the years the grave took. Take them from it... and the time is yours.
[fearful] Vonahlok. The Undoing. It keeps the last word, on the frozen peak of Mount Anthor.
Where it flies, death itself comes undone. It is the oldest of the three... and the angriest.
I felt it fall. SLEN is silent... the dead in the Reach are only bones again. You are stronger for it.
TIID is silent. The time the dead stole is yours now. [softly] Spend it better than they did.
[relieved] The Undoing has undone its last. I never thought I would hear VO go quiet.
Only their maker. On the summit of the Throat of the World, where we cast him out of time, his echo still circles.
It is not the World-Eater himself. Only the shape his voice left in the sky. [pause] It is enough to kill you.
Break it... and the curse breaks with it. Every grave in Skyrim will be quiet.

lines.ask: How do I beat the Echo?
lines.text: Bring everything you have earned. The wonder. The words you took from the three. And anyone who will stand with you.

lines.ask: How do I beat the Echo?
lines.text: It will call the dead of all Skyrim to the summit. Do not let them pull you away from it.
[softly] Here, it is. The echo is broken, and Skyrim's dead are sleeping again. The nights are only nights.
But the World-Eater himself still lives. Without his echo, he has nowhere left to hide... but Sovngarde.
[tense] He will go there to feed on the souls of the dead. That is where the last fight waits for you.

lines.ask: What is the Hall of the Awakened?
lines.text: A room beneath High Hrothgar that opened when the echo broke. The Tongues built it for whoever ended this.

lines.ask: What is the Hall of the Awakened?
lines.text: It is yours now. Go and see it.
[softly] The mill wheel turns, and no red light falls over the barrow. Listen... it is a quiet valley again.
This was the first stone you woke. I will remember that.

lines.ask: What was Riverwood like in your time?
lines.text: When we raised this stone, there was no town here. Only the river, and a dragon's nest on the mountain above it.
The Gildergreen is quiet. The plains are only grass again.
Nahkriin's gate has one less keeper. The road to Sovngarde is a little clearer for it.

lines.ask: What was Whiterun like in your time?
lines.text: The dragon in Dragonsreach was not the first caged on that hill. The first was there in our time. We heard it screaming for a year.
The arch over the sea is quiet. The bards can sing of the dead again, instead of to them.
[softly] Solitude will tell this story for a hundred years. They will get it wrong. Let them.

lines.ask: What was Solitude like in your time?
lines.text: There were Tongues who lived on these cliffs, and taught their students to shout across the water. The sea still remembers the sound.
The candle still burns, and nothing comes to it but the living.
Windhelm has buried enough of its own. It can rest now.

lines.ask: What was Windhelm like in your time?
lines.text: Ysgramor's people built over the stone without knowing it was here. It has listened to every king of Windhelm since.
The stone city is still. Even the Reach's oldest dead have gone back to sleep.
Otar is gone. I will not mourn him. Neither did his cult.

lines.ask: What was Markarth like in your time?
lines.text: The deep elves had a stone of their own, under the cliff. Ours answered it once. [softly] Nothing answers from down there now.
The canal is only water again. The thieves can go back to stealing from the living.
Rahgot's followers died for him twice. [softly] Let them stay dead this time.

lines.ask: What was Riften like in your time?
lines.text: The lake here was a holy place to Mara before there was a city. We raised the stone where her pilgrims rested.
The rows are quiet. Falkreath can bury its dead and leave them buried.
Krosis grieved for a thousand years. I hope he has stopped.

lines.ask: What was Falkreath like in your time?
lines.text: Even in our time, people came here to bury their dead. Some places are made for grief.
The fog is only fog again. Morthal can sleep with its doors unbarred.
Hevnoraak's servants were right to seal him. You finished what they started.

lines.ask: What was Morthal like in your time?
lines.text: The marsh swallowed the first stone we raised here. This is the second. We were careful where we put it.
The harbour is frozen and still. Tonight, Dawnstar will sleep without dreaming.
[softly] The nightmares are over here. For once, the dreamers will wake rested.

lines.ask: What was Dawnstar like in your time?
lines.text: There was a shrine in the hills here to a god of dreams. We built the stone well away from it. We were right to.
The storm has passed. The bridge to the College is only a bridge again.
Morokei is gone, and the College will claim the credit. Let it.

lines.ask: What was Winterhold like in your time?
lines.text: This stone once stood in a great city. The sea took the city. The stone held on. [softly] So did the College.
The stone offers four ways to fight the dead. The Tongues walked all of them, once.
The Summoner, who calls the dead's own kind to fight them. The Destruction mage, who burns them where they stand.
The Alchemist, who bottles every element and pours it out. The Spellsword, steel in one hand and a spell in the other.
Choose at the stone. Choosing again later costs dearly, so choose well.
The stone will let you. It will cost you fifty thousand of the essence the dead leave behind.
Your kit stays your own. But your path's powers stay with the path.

lines.ask: What do you see in me?
lines.text: You call things to fight for you, and they come. The Tongues had a word for people like you. It was not a kind word.

lines.ask: What do you see in me?
lines.text: [softly] But it was a useful one. The dead fear what does not fear them.

lines.ask: Teach me of the Summoner's craft.
lines.text: Let your servants hold the line. You are the one who must not fall. Without you, they go back where they came from.

lines.ask: Teach me of the Summoner's craft.
lines.text: The more you call, the thinner you are spread. Be wise about it.

lines.ask: Is there a wonder for my path?
lines.text: There is. The Soulcaller's Staff. But it sleeps, and it will not wake until six stones are free.
Listen... the ghost-cats that guarded the Tongues still prowl. Their souls are scattered. Gather them.
Follow them quietly at night, near a freed stone. They fear the hunter. They will come to a patient one.
The Soulcaller's Staff. Every soul it takes is one the dead will never get back.
At twenty souls the pride answers. [softly] They remember who freed them.

lines.ask: Did the Tongues fight like me?
lines.text: One of us could call the wolves down from the mountain with a word. They followed her to the summit. None of them came back.

lines.ask: What do you see in me?
lines.text: Fire. Frost. Storm. You do not ask the dead to sleep. You make them.

lines.ask: What do you see in me?
lines.text: [softly] The Tongues had mages like you. The dragons learned to fear them... for a while.

lines.ask: Teach me of the Destruction mage's craft.
lines.text: Your power is in your magicka, and your magicka runs out. Never let the dead catch you empty.

lines.ask: Teach me of the Destruction mage's craft.
lines.text: Each element has its use. Fire for the crowd. Frost to slow them. Storm for whatever is still standing.

lines.ask: Is there a wonder for my path?
lines.text: There is. The Wyrmspine Javelin. But it sleeps, and it will not wake until six stones are free.
A god's eye fell to Nirn, and the curse buried its light. The Eye of Magnus... its pieces are falling again.
When a star crosses the sky above you at night, strike it down. That is where the path begins.
The Wyrmspine Javelin. Carved from a dragon's spine, and it remembers the sky.
Throw it hard. It wants to fly again.

lines.ask: Did the Tongues fight like me?
lines.text: Our fire-callers burned the dragons' priests out of their towers. The dragons answered in kind. Fire was cheap in those days.

lines.ask: What do you see in me?
lines.text: You bottle what the rest of us fear. Fire in glass, frost in glass... [softly] even, one day, the curse itself.

lines.ask: What do you see in me?
lines.text: The Tongues never trusted alchemists. They trusted their potions well enough.

lines.ask: Teach me of the Alchemist's craft.
lines.text: Your flasks are your strength. Know which element the dead fear, and give them that one.

lines.ask: Teach me of the Alchemist's craft.
lines.text: Never stand still to brew. The dead do not wait for anything to cool.

lines.ask: Is there a wonder for my path?
lines.text: There is. The Mutagen Staff. But it sleeps, and it will not wake until six stones are free.
Every element can be bottled. Brew the Elixir of Aetherius... and the Mutagen Staff will answer you.
One of the dead burns brighter than the rest. Break it with glass... and catch what falls.
The Mutagen Staff. Six vials of the world's elements, poured through one orb.
The Elixir of Aetherius was only ever a story. You made it true.

lines.ask: Did the Tongues fight like me?
lines.text: We had a healer who brewed in a skull, because it was the only bowl she had. She kept more of us alive than the Voice did.

lines.ask: What do you see in me?
lines.text: Steel in one hand, a spell in the other. You fight the way the first Tongues fought, before they had the Voice.

lines.ask: What do you see in me?
lines.text: [softly] You get closer to the dead than anyone should. They feel it.

lines.ask: Teach me of the Spellsword's craft.
lines.text: Your blade carries your spell. Choose the spell before you choose the fight.

lines.ask: Teach me of the Spellsword's craft.
lines.text: Get close, and stay close. A Spellsword at the edge of a fight is only half of one.

lines.ask: Is there a wonder for my path?
lines.text: There is. The Dragon Slayer. But it sleeps, and it will not wake until six stones are free.
A slayer once swore an oath and broke his blade on the World-Eater's scales. The pieces are scattered.
Take up his oath. Where the World-Eater first returned, a broken blade waits for a hand. Begin there.
The Dragon Slayer. Every blow carries the spell in your other hand.
The slayer's oath is kept. [softly] He would have been glad of you.

lines.ask: Did the Tongues fight like me?
lines.text: Before the Voice, we had steel and a little magic, and we fought dragons with that. Most of us died. The ones who lived taught the rest.
Each of you walks a path of your own. Together, you are what the Tongues were. [softly] Stay together.
If one of you falls, the rest of you lift them. The dead do not take prisoners.
[whispers] ...someone who has waited... too long... wake another stone...
Someone who was here when these stones were raised. That is all I can give you... for now.
[softly] My name is in the mist with everything else. Wake more stones, and it will come back to me.
Far. Behind the mist he left across the road to Sovngarde. I speak through the stones because I cannot speak any other way.
Older than your Empire. Older than the first Nord kings. They were raised while dragons still ruled the sky.
We raised them in secret, in the dark, where the dragons' priests would not see.
The three of us. The first who learned the Voice... and turned it on our masters.
One fell at the summit, before the end. One I have not seen since. And I... I am still here.
[sad] A warrior with a golden hilt. She was the bravest of us. She went at him first, and he took her first.
I watched her fall. I did not stop. [softly] That is what she would have wanted.
A warrior with one eye, who saw more than most with two. After the summit... I lost him in the mist.
Perhaps he is in Sovngarde, waiting for the road to open. I hope so.
Six stones are free... and I remember. I am Felldir. Felldir the Old.
[softly] It has been a very long time since anyone asked me that.

lines.ask: What did you do at the summit?
lines.text: I read the Elder Scroll. The others held him in the sky, and I read it... and the World-Eater was cast out of time.

lines.ask: What did you do at the summit?
lines.text: We thought it was the end. We were young. We did not know that time has a way of giving things back.
I lived a long life after the summit, and died old, and took the road to Sovngarde. When he shouted at Helgen, the mist fell over it... with me still on it.
I cannot go forward, and I will not go back. So I wait... and I speak through the stones we raised.

lines.ask: Have you been alone all this time?
lines.text: [sad] The dead pass me in the mist. They cannot see the way. Neither can I. We are all lost together.

lines.ask: Have you been alone all this time?
lines.text: Then you came. [softly] The first living voice I have heard in a very long time.
Proud. Patient. He did not hate us. You do not hate the grass you walk on.
That is what frightened me most. Not his anger... his certainty.

lines.ask: Did you know there would be a Dragonborn?
lines.text: We hoped. The Scroll told us he would come back. It did not tell us who would be waiting when he did.

lines.ask: Did you know there would be a Dragonborn?
lines.text: [softly] I am glad it was you.

lines.ask: Who are the Greybeards to you?
lines.text: They came after us. They took the Voice and made it quiet, and climbed the mountain to keep it safe.

lines.ask: Who are the Greybeards to you?
lines.text: We used it to fight. They use it to listen. [softly] Perhaps they are wiser than we were.
I did. For a long time. Then I was dead for longer than I was ever alive, and hate is hard to carry that far.
Now I only want them to stop. That is not the same thing.
To go home. Nothing more. They are not cruel... they are lost, and the World-Eater's voice is all they can hear.
[sad] When you put them down, you are not killing them. You are showing them the way.

lines.ask: What will happen to you now?
lines.text: [softly] I go back into the mist, to wait with the others. A golden hilt... and one eye. They are there. I can feel them.

lines.ask: What will happen to you now?
lines.text: When you come to Sovngarde, we will be waiting. Three old voices, ready to shout beside you one more time.

lines.ask: What will happen to you now?
lines.text: [softly] Thank you, Dragonborn. Until Sovngarde.
Listen... the ghost-cats that guarded the Tongues still prowl. Gather their scattered souls, and the Soulcaller's Staff will answer you.
Three spirit cats stalk the edges of this city by moonlight. They fear the hunter. Come to them quietly.
Three souls pad behind you now.
A pride must hunt. Let your servants kill thirty of the dead tonight, and keep the spirit at your side alive.
The pride has tasted the hunt.
Four stones remember the pride's roar. Listen to the order they call, then answer them.
The roar is whole again.
Stand at this altar while the dead come. Lift no blade. Let only what you call do the killing.
The den is ready.
The Bone-Caller chains the Old King's soul. Break the chains, then break him.
The Old King runs free.
The pride is whole. The Greybeards are calling. The Soulcaller's Staff waits at High Hrothgar.
A god's eye fell to Nirn, and the curse buried its light. Wake its fire, frost and storm, and the Wyrmspine Javelin is yours to claim.
Three seals sleep near this altar: ember, rime and storm. Strike each with its own element, before the first goes dark again.
The seals are open.
Pieces of the Eye are falling tonight. Catch five before they burn out.
The light is gathered.
Four stones, four colours. Ember before frost, frost before storm, and storm before the sun. Strike them so.
The prism shines.
Burn forty of the dead tonight. Fire, frost and storm... the Eye hungers for all three.
The Eye is kindled.
The Great Anomaly wears every element in turn. Strike it with what it fears, never with what it wears.
The Anomaly is unmade.
The Eye sees again. The Greybeards are calling. The Wyrmspine Javelin waits at High Hrothgar.
Every element can be bottled... even the curse. Brew the Elixir of Aetherius, and the Mutagen Staff will be yours.
Six of the dead rise tonight, each wrapped in an element. Answer each with its own flask, and take what falls.
Six essences. Carry them carefully.
A crucible needs an altar's fire. Bring the essences here before dawn.
The crucible is lit.
Four braziers flicker a formula. Copy it with your flasks, in the order they burn.
The formula holds.
The brew must not be shaken. Hold this altar against the dead, and do not bleed.
The Elixir is settling.
The Matriarch drinks whatever strikes her. Never feed her the same element twice.
The Matriarch is spent.
The Elixir is brewed. The Greybeards are calling. The Mutagen Staff waits at High Hrothgar.
A slayer swore an oath and broke his blade on Alduin's scales. Take up his oath, and the Dragon Slayer will be yours.
The ground near this altar is hallowed. Feed it thirty of the dead, slain where it glows.
The ground is fed.
Five shards of the old blade lie scattered tonight. Their guardians wake when you come near.
The blade is gathered.
Four rune-stones sing in turn. Strike them with steel, in the order they sing.
The runes remember the blade.
Swear the oath in steel. Forty of the dead by your blade, a spell ready in your other hand.
The oath is sworn.
Thorgar the Skulltaker holds the hilt. Magic will not touch him. Face him with the blade alone.
The hilt is yours.
The blade is whole. The Greybeards are calling. The Dragon Slayer waits at High Hrothgar.
The wonders still sleep. Free more cities, and they will stir.
The next whisper waits...
...where the mill wheel turns beside the river, over the hill from where the dragon first broke the sky.
...beneath the hall built on a dragon's cage, where the golden tree grows.
...where the great arch spans the sea, and the bards keep their songs.
...in the oldest city of stone, where the snow never leaves the palace of kings.
...in the city the deep elves carved, where the cliffs bleed silver.
...where the canals run beneath a city of thieves and honey.
...among the graves in the pines, where the dead outnumber the living.
...in the marsh town, where the mist hides what walks.
...on the cold northern shore, where the dreamers cannot sleep.
...where the city fell into the sea, and the college stands alone.
A lone spirit walks the night. Follow it softly... and see where it leads.
When a star crosses the sky above you... strike it down.
One of the dead burns brighter than the rest. Break it with glass, and catch what falls.
Where the World-Eater first returned, a broken blade waits for a hand.
Two stones wake... so you can hear me. These altars were old before your Empire was born. They were raised while dragons still ruled the sky.
We raised them, the three of us... the first who learned the Voice and turned it on its masters. One fell at the summit. One I have not seen since. And I... I am still here.
Six stones are free... you may hear my name. I am Felldir the Old. I read the Scroll that cast Alduin out of time, and I wait for you behind his mist. The wonders stir... watch the night.
